chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from his father, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Ḥannāṭ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said:

I complained to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about what I was suffering from pains, and I was frequently ill. So he said to me: “O ʿAbd Allāh, if the believer knew what reward he has in afflictions, he would wish that he had been cut with scissors.”

key_terms.مِسْقَامًا: frequently ill or prone to sickness

ai.seo_question: What reward does a believer receive for afflictions and illness?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the believer’s afflictions carry immense reward with Allah. It encourages patience in suffering by showing that, if the true recompense were known, even severe pain would be seen as small compared to its reward.
